newsitem.title: UK: Technicals bow to EMU trades as BTPs target 138.00.
newsitem.headline: Technicals bow to EMU trades as BTPs target 138.00.

text.p: The blistering rally in Italian bond futures has left technical indicators hugely overbought, but with EMU convergence trades calling the shots analysts said the market should have no problem reaching 138.00 near term.
Once BTPs do peak however, the correction will be savage, they added on Wednesday, with the market shedding at least four or five points in a matter of days.
"We're getting to ridiculous levels -- the nine-day Relative Strength Index is at 87 percent," said Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at London Bond Broking here.
"But nevertheless, we can probably get a bit further."
He said in pure spread terms, even if the German market is unchanged, a 10-year BTP/Bund gap of 75 basis points meant another point and a half on the Italian future.
"That would give us 138.00 which would definitely be the upper limit in the short term," he said.
September BTPs have surged almost eight points since the 129.07 low on June 10. By 1000 GMT, they were up 57 basis points at 136.83, off a new record high earlier of 136.94.
The 10-year BTP/Bund spread was at 93 basis points, down from 117 basis points just over a week ago.
Even the 10-year cash yield has broken through the 6.50 percent psychological barrier. By 1000 GMT the 6.75 percent bond due February 2007 was yielding 6.46 percent.
"When the momentum is so strong, you end up trying to call the top of the market the whole time because it's so severely overbought," said Ostwald.
But he added he would not sell the market just yet, but wait for it to push slightly higher.
"My best guess is 138.00, and from there I'm looking for a retracement down to the 133.00 level pretty quickly," he said.
Ostwald noted a 50 percent retracement of the rally since June would give a target level of 132.82.
Daniele Castelnuovo, an analyst at Banca Euromobiliare in Milan, was even more optimistic.
He expected the September BTP to reach the lofty heights of 140.00 within the next 10 days.
"The uptrend is strong and the ultimate target is 140.00. I don't see any reason for any retracement for the time being," he said.
Castelnuovo agreed European economic and monetary union (EMU) convergence trades and a buoyant U.S. Treasury market were the driving forces behind the BTPs' rally.
"The only risk is an unforeseeable fall in U.S. T-bonds which could impair the general uptrend of European markets," he said.
Analysts at MCM YieldWatch in London said hourly studies suggested the market would push to 137.05, a Fibonacci projection level, with the potential for a pull back from there.
"However, over the short term, the potential is still seen for further gains towards 137.71," they said in a note for clients.
Ostwald noted most of the buying interest at current levels was professional rather than retail.
"One worrying thing is there's not a lot of retail involved, it's traders pushing the market up," he said.
-- Jennifer Scott, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 8682
